I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I would keep to the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At 70, I would not spread myself across too many crops or choose anything management-heavy like vegetables or cotton. My education is high, so I am comfortable using improved seed, calibrated fertilization, and disciplined field timing, but I still want a plan that is stable, familiar, and low-risk. Wheat-maize rotation fits my land, climate, machinery, and labor capacity better than anything else.

I would plant winter wheat on all of my land for the cool season, then harvest it and follow immediately with summer maize. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I value reliable establishment, stronger yield, and better stress tolerance. I would keep fertilizer rates moderate to strong, because I want to support yield without wasting input. I would use rotary tillage for wheat after maize residue is handled, and for summer maize I would prefer no-tillage direct seeding after wheat harvest to save time and conserve soil moisture. Irrigation would stay limited but timely, since water matters most at key growth stages. I would not spray on a calendar just to spray; I would keep applications to a practical number aimed at weeds, diseases, and insects only when they are likely to matter. My goal would be a clean, manageable, wheat-maize year with solid yields and low operational strain.
